summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn opens a new child of the conf-change line after a construction-time probe surfaced it: an attempt to drive the Node API of a removed member hit raft.applyConfChange's panic, so I traced the mechanism and registered question @confchange_remove_last_voter (parent b87d04b254e44ceaadb200304929056a-question-0) with a sourced Behavior entry and an experiment. Source trace: the changer computes the resulting configuration and returns the error 'removed all voters' when no voter remains (confchange/confchange.go:170-172, treated as an expected changer-level rejection in confchange/testdata/simple_safety.txt), the leader's propose-time validation checks pending and joint state but never the resulting voter set (raft.go:1318-1335), and applyConfChange converts any changer error into a panic with a TODO to return it to the caller (raft.go:1961-1964) - so a legal proposal can be accepted, committed, and then abort the applying node. The experiment proposes a ConfChangeV2 removing the only voter on a single-voter leader through the real MsgProp path, confirms the entry committed, then applies it through the documented application path with the panic recovered verbatim, using an add-voter change of the same shape as the control; two comparisons encode the duty that the apply path must not abort the node (expected violated for the removal, expected holds for the control). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, that the proposal returns no error and commits at the new index while applying it panics with the changer's own 'removed all voters' text and leaves the configuration unchanged, whereas the control applies cleanly. Limitations state the single-voter scope, the recovered-panic framing and the fact that process-level and restart consequences are inferred; the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
